Q: How to extract Amazon Reviews? A:

Scraping reviews on Amazon has gotten a lot harder but if you just need the data you can use a free service like https://amzshark.com and download reviews based on keywords or specific products in CSV, JSON, XLSX etc

Q: How do I revive vibe code that was automated by Claude A:

if it doesn't find the last price of a stock, it assumes a certain price and then just places an order.

On the basis of what? How is that price determined then? Why can't it find the last price, is it due to lack of history, or the price cannot be retrieved for some technical reason? Would be interesting to know.

This is trading, you could lose a lot of money so I don't understand that you would put that thing in production without a third-party review first.

  • Write good specs, that's what drives the result
  • Read the code, if you don't understand it, ask AI to explain
  • Ask AI to comment the code, so that assumptions are outlined clearly
  • Ask more experienced people to review the code, pay for the code review if necessary
  • Add some guardrails, limit the amount of money that can be spent

AI cannot guess everything, or decide what is desirable in every situation.

Some unit tests can help validate the behavior of the code, but you need to think about edge cases.

That's why vibe coding cannot replace programmers, programmers know what questions to ask, what issues to anticipate and they have experience, so there is plenty of rookie mistakes they won't make because it's obvious to them. You pay for their expertise, to have something more solid and less risky to use in return.

Likewise, you could use AI to draft a contract (or a lawsuit), but you'd rather hire a lawyer to ensure that the document will stand in front of a court.

Q: Stripping quoted/replied content from HTML email bodies across clients with regex. which markers am I missing and where will it break? A:

I don't know about the other ones but you can combine the first 4.
When matched check the capture groups to see which matched:

Group 2 = div, id = appendonsend
Group 3 = div, id = divRplyFwdMsg
Group 4 = div, id = Signature
Group 6 = blockquote, type = cite

https://regex101.com/r/VN1VT9/1

(?i)(?:<div(?=\s)(?=(?:[^>"']|"[^"]*"|'[^']*')*?\sid\s*=\s*(?:(['"])(?:(?!\1)[\S\s])*?(?:(appendonsend)|(divRplyFwdMsg)|(Signature))(?:(?!\1)[\S\s])*\1)(?:"[\S\s]*?"|'[\S\s]*?'|[^>]?)*?>)\s+(?:"[\S\s]*?"|'[\S\s]*?'|[^>]?)+>|<blockquote(?=\s)(?=(?:[^>"']|"[^"]*"|'[^']*')*?\stype\s*=\s*(?:(['"])(?:(?!\5)[\S\s])*?(cite)(?:(?!\5)[\S\s])*\5)(?:"[\S\s]*?"|'[\S\s]*?'|[^>]?)*?>)\s+(?:"[\S\s]*?"|'[\S\s]*?'|[^>]?)+>)

 (?:

Q: How do Bluetooth speakers, headsets, and devices exchange battery level information? (especially with an Android device) A:

Bluetooth audio devices generally implement HFP (Hands-Free Profile), which among other things provides battery information. This is unrelated to GATT and BLE. It's a "classic" (BR/EDR) profile. Headsets are fundamentally "classic" devices. They are not "low-energy" devices, even though many audio devices today also implement BLE control protocols (often custom). (*)

Some devices do support the GATT Battery Service, but it would be a device-by-device thing. More commonly, if audio devices advertise their battery over BLE, it will be part of a custom protocol in order to work with their own app, rather than using a standard service. (This is how most of the earbuds I've worked on behave.)

On Linux, I believe you'll use oFono for this.

On Android, you can access the AG role of HFP using BluetoothHeadset. For an introduction, see How to use bluetooth HFP profile in android programmatically? (I know you probably won't need this, but future searchers may be solving similar problems on Android.)

There is no equivalent on iOS. You cannot access HFP or most other classic profiles on iOS at all. The OS implements them (so your Linux tool would be able to interoperate), but does not provide any public APIs on iOS.

(*) There is a new technology called LE-Audio, but, like so many things in Bluetooth, it is yet another completely separate thing. I suspect that CAP devices, which LE-Audio relies on, will also generally provide the LE Battery Service, but I haven't worked with any of them to know.

Q: Android Studio not found AndroidManifest.xml A:

You can configure the location of the manifest file like this:

  1. open the Project Structure dialog
  2. go to "Modules" (in the left tree)
  3. select "Android" in the middle column of the dialog
  4. Now you see on the right side a list of files where you can pick the Manifest file.

Q: Authoritative engine Id and context engine id in snmp v3 A:

I think -3e for (security) engine ID and -3E for context engine ID should do the trick for snmptrapd.conf. I found these in the net-snmp source in snmplib/snmpv3.c:150 for reference, not really sure if they are documented.

I think that is what you're asking for? You may need to play with the net-snmp source and step through things if snmptrapd doesn't behave correctly.
